title: Reading data questions: tables, totals and percentages
subtitle: A Kuphanda revision guide for MSCE Mathematics

blocks.text: Data questions look easy until the marks are lost on a total that does not add up, or a percentage taken of the wrong number. Almost every error in this topic comes from reading the table carelessly rather than from the arithmetic itself. Read the row headings, the column headings, and the units before you touch a calculator.
Table 1: monthly sales at a school tuck shop, in Malawi kwacha.

blocks.label: Check the total first
blocks.text: If a total row is given, add one column in your head before you answer anything. If your sum disagrees with the printed total, the printed total is what the next part of the question depends on.

items: Percentage of a total: divide the part by the total, then multiply by 100.
Percentage change: divide the change by the original amount, not the new one.
Mean of grouped data: multiply each value by its frequency, add, then divide by the total frequency.
Always write the unit — MWK, kg, litres — or the answer reads as a bare number.

blocks.text: The tuck shop records in Table 1 show sales for the first three months of the year.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Calculate the total sales for the three months.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: What percentage of the total sales came from drinks? Give your answer to one decimal place.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Stationery sales rose from January to March. Calculate the percentage increase.

items: (c) The increase is 16 000 − 12 000 = 4 000. As a percentage of January: 4 000 ÷ 12 000 × 100 = 33.3%.

blocks.text: A class of 40 learners recorded how many books they read in a term.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Show that the total number of learners is 40.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Calculate the mean number of books read per learner.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: What percentage of the class read 3 or more books?

items: A mean may be a decimal — 1.95 books is a correct mean even though nobody read 1.95 books.
For percentage change the original amount always goes underneath. Dividing by the new amount is the most common mistake in this topic.
If a question says 'hence', it wants your previous answer, not a fresh start.

blocks.text: Mark your own work against the table, not against the final number: most marks in data questions are for the intermediate value, so a wrong final answer with correct working still scores.
